title: Compiler diagnostics are structured only at the external CLI boundary
observed_need: Compile-fail and diagnostic tests must match diagnostic identity and preserve source spans without scraping human prose.
current_language_behavior: The Rust toolchain exposes versioned structured diagnostics and the native runner fail-closes on invalid admission. P-062 added a Test-owned MNCS application that projects diagnostic codes and applies compile verdict policy without building a host diagnostic-code list. P-063 replaces the verdict application's Test JsonValue tree projection with bounded Stdlib JSON cursor events and a syntax validator. P-064 added bounded native typed records for standard diagnostic objects; P-065 extended them with expected tokens and one level of related diagnostics. P-066 replaced the diagnostic projector's JsonValue tree traversal with a second bounded json_cursor pass over the original chunked bytes. P-067 retires the fixed native diagnostic-record array and Python reconstruction mapper: MNCS validates the selected array and returns its source span, then Python decodes only that selected span for the public dictionary contract. MNCS application code still cannot directly consume compiler Diagnostic values.
why_insufficient: P-067 removes the fixed intermediate diagnostic record tree and full-document Python parse on supported inputs, but Python still decodes the selected bounded JSON array into public dictionaries. Unsupported value types, deeper or oversized structures, execution-budget exhaustion, and oversized documents still use Python's compatibility parser; all paths still cross the structured CLI JSON boundary.
minimal_reproducer: tests/fixtures/compile_fail.mncs plus tools/mncs_test.py: compile_entry sends the raw document to native/mncs/test/compile_diagnostic_verdict_v1.mncs, which validates the bounded document and selects the diagnostic-array span before Python decodes that span for the established public result.
desired_direction: A versioned diagnostic value/protocol exposing code, severity, source span, related diagnostics, and rendered forms to native tooling.
workaround: The Test-owned native application validates up to 16,384 bytes with the Stdlib JSON cursor and syntax scanner, applies compile verdict policy, and returns the byte span for up to 32 standard diagnostics from the selected root, errors, or diagnostics array. Python decodes only that validated span to preserve the public dictionary contract. Shapes outside the bounded projection retain the Python compatibility parser; no formatted-stderr parsing is used.
